status: TOOLING WIN + PARTIAL LAW. New `pokeview` harness phase captures a reproducible blit call-list for ANY (gx,gy,facing) in zone 0 (poke the party DGROUP fields to the target cell, serialize, capture an in-place turn recompose at ega.drv FUN_0a93). Captured 4 DISTINCT views (gy121-f0 reference, gy119-f0 door-near, gx127-f3 parity-odd-decoration, gx126gy117-f0 blocked-front-decoration) + cross-referenced each against level-0 cell-data. CHARACTERIZED the placement-table structure (depth-banked ceiling/floor twins, per-depth side/corner/door families, constant top-strip chrome) and the two BLIT laws that ARE byte-exact: (1) the OR-vs-MASKED branch is selected by FRAME PARITY (gx+gy+facing)%2 — even=>direct OR blits, odd=>whole-frame horizontal-mirror via the masked branch; (2) the masked branch is a HORIZONTAL MIRROR about page-byte column 20 (screen px 160): src.destX + dst.destX + dst.w == 40 for EVERY masked pair (19/19 in V3, all pairs in V1/V2/V4). NOT cracked: the per-depth (slot-code,depth)->placement-index arithmetic still lives in the decompiler-resistant slot helpers (wmaze 0x3828/0x3c11/0x3dce/0x4892); no reproducing function. Also found: for parity-ODD / blocked-front views the masked src->dst PAIRING + ORDER OSCILLATE run-to-run (mid-build), so only the placement-index SET, the OR list, the pass LENGTH, and the mirror law are deterministic for those — the exact ordered pairing is NOT.

findings.claim: FRAME PARITY = (gx+gy+facing)%2 selects the blit BRANCH for (nearly) the WHOLE frame. PARITY EVEN (V1 gx127gy121f0 par0: 27 OR/4 masked; V2 gx127gy119f0 par0: 30 OR/4 masked): the perspective pieces are drawn by DIRECT forward OR-blits (arg10==0xffff), with only the 4 near side-panel mirrors going through the masked branch. PARITY ODD (V3 gx127gy121f3 par1: 7 OR/27 masked; V4 gx126gy117f0 par1: 6 OR/7 masked): essentially the ENTIRE frame is drawn through the MASKED (horizontal-mirror) branch — the same pieces, mirrored. The only OR calls that survive in a parity-odd frame are the 6 top-strip chrome pieces (346/349/352/355/358/361) plus any thin asymmetric decoration (V3's idx114). This is the BLIT-LEVEL manifestation of the classify-stage parity-alternation law (maze-classify-projection.json parity-alternation-not-geometry): the engine pre-mirrors the right half by toggling the whole compose between forward-OR and mirror-masked on parity.

findings.claim: The MASKED branch is a HORIZONTAL MIRROR of the source placement about page-byte column 20 (= screen pixel 160, the viewport horizontal center). For every masked call (src=arg0c, dst=arg10): dst.destX + src.destX + dst.w == 40 (page row = 40 bytes). Self-symmetric center pieces map to themselves (e.g. 123->123: destX 13, w14, 13+13+14=40; 124->124: 16+16+8=40). Left/right pieces swap (134@destX9 <-> 138@destX27; 162@9 <-> 166@27). VERIFIED for ALL masked pairs: 19/19 in V3, 4/4 in V1, 4/4 in V2, all in V4. This is the byte-exact geometry of the masked-mirror branch (consistent with maze-masked-mirror's prior masked-GEOMETRY gate).

evidence.details: For each masked call, src/dst placement records read from the live cs:[0x190] placement table at capture time. Law dst.destX + src.destX + dst.w == 40 holds universally. V1: 13->4 (24+8+8=40), 10->7, 7->10, 4->13. V2: 33->30 (16+22+2=40), 30->33, 24->24, 27->27. V3 cross-pairs e.g. 134->138 (27+9+4=40), 162->166, 131->143, etc — 19/19. Page row stride = 40 bytes (320px/8).

findings.claim: The placement table is organized into DEPTH-BANKED families that the wmaze depth loop (0x4c60) indexes per depth (0..3, back-to-front). Confirmed families from the union of 4 views' live records: (1) CEILING strips 122/123/124/125 = depths 0/1/2/3, destRow 32/39/51/59, w 18/14/8/4, destX converging 11/13/16/18 (perspective). (2) FLOOR TWIN = ceiling idx + 28 (122->150, 123->151, 124->152, 125->153; destRow 128/104/88/83 — the mirrored vertical). (3) SIDE/CORNER pieces per depth: a left cluster (destX 9/13) and right cluster (destX 24/27/21/22), e.g. 131/135/139/143 (+ floor twins 159/163/167/171) at the door-recess depths, 133/137/141/145 (+161/165/169/173) shallower. (4) NEAR full-height walls 15/19 (img3/img7, w4 h112) emitted when bounded at d0/d1. (5) TOP-STRIP chrome 346/349/352/355/358/361 (stride 3, destRow 7, w2 h16) — ALWAYS emitted, all 6, in EVERY view (the screen-top band). Every full call list has the shape [122, 150, <per-depth wall/decoration pieces back-to-front>, <6 top strips>]. The leading 122/150 (d0 ceiling+floor) and trailing 6 strips are constant; the middle is the depth-loop emit selected by per-depth cell-data.

findings.claim: The per-depth CELL-DATA (forward-edge code + side solidity + special4 decoration) selects WHICH piece families emit at each depth — the SELECTION half of the generation law. Cross-referenced (cell-data depth profiles via the FORWARD edge read N/W per facing + lateral-neighbour side reads, per the classify projection): V1 fwdEdge profile [0,0,3,0] (door code 3 at depth2) -> emits the deep door-recess family (131/135/139/143 + twins) at the mid depths + the small far door pieces (2/85/89). V2 fwdEdge [0,3,0,0] (door code 3 at depth1, CLOSER) -> emits the near full-height walls (15/19) + a LARGER door-frame family (133/137/141/145, 136/140 + twins) — the same door rendered bigger because it is one depth nearer. V4 fwdEdge [2,2,0,2] (SOLID front at depth0, blocked) -> the frame fills with the near wall via the mirror branch (img0 idx0/9 w14 h87) + ceiling/floor + the 6 strips, total only 13 calls (a near wall occludes the deeper pieces). V3 (facing3, sp4=7 at d1 to the left) -> emits the thin decoration column idx114. So: forward-edge code (open/solid/door) at each depth gates the wall/door family; special4 decoration adds the decoration piece; a solid near edge occludes deeper depths (fewer total calls). This is the classify slot-code (maze-classify-projection.json) feeding the placement-index arithmetic.

findings.claim: For parity-ODD and blocked-front views, the masked src->dst PAIRING and the call ORDER OSCILLATE run-to-run (the in-place recompose is mid-build / not fully settled), so they are NOT deterministic. Across 3 V4 captures the masked pairing varied ([150->122,15->0,...] vs [122->134,0->6,...] vs [15->150,138->19,...]) and across 2 V3 captures the masked head moved phase. What IS deterministic for these views: the placement-index SET (V4 always {0,6,9,15,19,122,134,138,150,162,166} + OR {346,349,352,355,358,361}), the pass LENGTH (V4 always 13, V3 always 34), the OR list, and the horizontal-mirror law (every pairing variant still satisfies destX+destX+w==40). For parity-EVEN open views (V1) the full ordered list IS byte-reproducible. CAVEAT for any reproducing function: validate parity-odd views by the SET + mirror law + length, not the exact ordered pairing.

evidence.details: V4 captured 3x: period (head-recurrence gap) = 13 every time; masked-pair SET identical; ordered pairing different each run. V1 captured 2x: OR list byte-identical. generation_pattern_summary.call_list_shape: [ceiling_d0 (122), floor_d0 (150), <depth-loop emit, back-to-front: per-depth ceiling 122+d / floor 150+d / side+corner+door families selected by that depth's cell-data>, <6 constant top-strips 346/349/352/355/358/361>].
generation_pattern_summary.branch_selection: parity = (gx+gy+facing)%2. EVEN => direct forward OR-blits (arg10==0xffff). ODD => whole-frame horizontal-mirror via the masked branch (arg10 = the mirror-image placement of the source arg0c).
generation_pattern_summary.masked_mirror_geometry: BYTE-EXACT: for a masked call src->dst, dst.destX + src.destX + dst.w == 40 (mirror about page-byte col 20 / screen px 160). Self-symmetric center pieces map to themselves.
generation_pattern_summary.depth_banks: ceiling = 122+d (d=0..3); floor twin = ceiling+28; per-depth side/corner pieces in left (destX 9/13) and right (destX 24/27/21/22) clusters; near full-height walls 15/19; constant top strips 346..361 (stride 3).
generation_pattern_summary.selection_inputs: per-depth forward-edge code (open 0 / solid 2 / door 1|3) gates wall+door family; special4 adds the decoration piece (e.g. sp4=7 -> column idx114); a solid near edge occludes deeper depths (shorter list).
generation_pattern_summary.what_is_unpinned: RESOLVED 2026-06-08, see docs/re/findings/maze-index-arithmetic.json + maze-gate-seeding.json. The index arithmetic is `placementIndex = base + depth`, with `base` a compile-time IMM argument pushed at each emit call site (NOT slot-code-keyed arithmetic). Frame parity [0x521a] picks which of a left/right base pair becomes the OR arg0c vs the mirror arg10. Pinned by hand-disasm of the EMIT fns (wall_emit_quad 0x406c / wall_emit_corner 0x45b4 / top_strips 0x4a15) — the slot helpers (0x3828 etc) only CLASSIFY + seed gates, they don't compute the index. Validated byte-exact vs the captured liveRecords. The OCCLUSION-STOP (which depths emit ceiling/floor) is also CRACKED (maze-gate-seeding.json): visible = [0..stop], stop = first depth whose forward edge OCCLUDES (front==2 OR front==3 with BOTH corners solid = a closed doorway) — byte-exact for v1/v2/v5/v6 incl. the v1-vs-v2 door-cap difference. A pure generateCallist(block,party) (callist.ts) emits the ceiling/floor skeleton + 6 strips from the maze block + party (no captured frame). STILL UNPINNED (medium): the per-depth GATE-SEEDING map for the SIDE/CORNER/DOOR-RECESS families (the per-slot gate bits seeded in 0x3931/0x3946/0x3951; a single family-base fires at multiple perspective depths).

concerns: The in-place poked recompose is a DIRTY recompose (per #077): it emits the full placement SELECTION but may drop the single deepest sub-pixel door-leaf detail (the 18px residual). That residual is a sub-placement draw-path gap, NOT a missing placement, so the SELECTION + geometry characterization is unaffected. Do not use these lists to chase the deep-door 100% gate.

For parity-odd / blocked-front views the masked PAIRING + ORDER are non-deterministic run-to-run; only the index SET, pass LENGTH, OR list, and mirror law are reliable. Any validation of a future reproducing function against these views must use the SET + mirror law, not the exact ordered pairing.

The reloc OR-blit base was a stable 0x6ba10 across fresh boots this pass, but it is heap-dependent in principle — the resolver re-derives it per run (WIZ6_ORBASE only short-circuits when known). The in-place left/right resolver can fail at some facings (V3 needed the override); a more robust forward-walk resolver is a follow-up.

Cell-data profiles use the classify edge-read law (maze-classify-projection.json) which is HIGH confidence for open/solid but MEDIUM for door-shape codes — the family<->depth index mapping inherits that medium confidence.
